newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel cabinet approves forex reforms.
newsitem.headline: Israel cabinet approves forex reforms.

text.p: Israel's cabinet approved on Wednesday key foreign currency reforms in a late-night session that ended with the resignation of Finance Minister Dan Meridor.

The Bank of Israel said the cabinet had voted to approve a widening of the shekel trading band to 15 percent from seven percent, adopting a compromise proposal by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu which Meridor had opposed.
The plan also called for implementing two sloping mid-points for the exchange rate band.

The lower end of the band will be adjusted according to a slope of four percent while the upper band will continue to be pegged against a six percent diagonal, the central bank said in a statement after the seven-hour cabinet meeting.

"The Bank of Israel emphasises that the changes in the sliding band by themselves will not have any influence on the exchange rate of the shekel against the basket of foreign currencies," it said in the statement.
"These changes in the rates are dependent, of course, on trading trends in foreign currency in Israel and exchange rates on international markets," the bank said.
Meridor had strongly opposed widening the shekel's trading bands, fearing it would lead to a further appreciation of the Israeli currency, hurt exports and cause the economy to slow.
Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel had pushed for expanding the bands, hoping to give the central bank some relief from the need to intervene constantly in the currency market.
High interest rates have caused the shekel to appreciate, forcing the bank to buy massive amounts of dollars to rein in the shekel.
